title: Formal Mechanised Semantics of CHERI C: Capabilities, Undefined Behaviour, and Provenance
problem: Memory safety vulnerabilities in C persist because existing semantics lack formal specifications for capability-based security mechanisms. CHERI C replaces machine-word pointers with unforgeable hardware capabilities, requiring formal mechanised semantics to precisely specify capability operations, undefined behavior handling, and pointer provenance.
motivation: Formal, machine-checked semantics are essential to verify that CHERI capabilities actually provide claimed security guarantees and enable safe adoption in security-critical systems.
method: The paper develops formal mechanised semantics for CHERI C by specifying how capabilities operate, derive from existing capabilities, and interact with undefined behavior and pointer provenance. The mechanised specification enables machine-checked verification of security properties and correct implementation in compilers like Clang/LLVM and GCC.
key_novelty: First formal mechanised semantics for a capability-based C dialect with rigorous specifications of capability operations, undefined behavior, and provenance in a machine-verifiable framework.
contributions: Formal mechanised semantics for CHERI C covering capability operations and derivation rules
Rigorous specification of undefined behavior within capability-based memory model
Formalization of pointer provenance tracking for capabilities
Foundation for machine-checked verification of CHERI compiler implementations and security properties

metrics.other: Mechanised specification coverage and formal verification completeness

limitations: The abstract does not discuss evaluation on actual systems, implementation overhead, or full coverage of CHERI features in the mechanised semantics.
primary_theme: Formal semantics of capability-based C security
